title: NBC News: Pentagon Weighs Pulling 25,000–40,000 Troops From Europe in Biggest Drawdown Since Cold War
detail: NBC News reported on September 17, 2026, citing seven current and former US and Western officials, that the Pentagon is weighing options to pull planes, ships, weapons and tens of thousands of troops out of Europe despite NATO allies' warnings about growing Russian aggression. The reduction under consideration could be roughly one-third of the roughly 80,000 US troops currently in Europe (about 25,000), though some options go as high as half, or up to 40,000 — which would mark the most significant scaling back of the US military presence in Europe since the aftermath of the Cold War. Germany, Italy and Spain, which host some of the largest US deployments, are among the countries most likely to be affected. The options are part of the six-month Pentagon force-posture review; Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, who heads US European Command and serves as NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, was expected to give Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth an initial analysis the following day (Friday, September 18) — the virtual briefing with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby confirmed in NATO's own readout of that date. NBC stressed no final decisions had been made, and the four full sets of troop-level options remain due to Hegseth by November 6 ahead of a December completion deadline.

media.caption: US troops rotate through Poland amid a Pentagon review that could pull tens of thousands of American forces from Europe
